text:
I’m proud to highlight Dr. Jerry Turner, a disabled U.S. Marine Corps 6842 veteran who served our country during the Gulf War from 1987 to 1993. Dr. Turner answered the call to serve and now he lives with the injuries that came with it. I’m pleased to report that Dr. Turner receives the full VA disability compensation he earned. 

Not every veteran in his family is treated the same way. Dr. Turner is married to a disabled, retired U.S. Navy veteran who completed a full military career and retired honorably, yet his retirement pay was reduced because of the injuries he sustained in service. Two disabled veterans can carry comparable injuries, and the one who served a full career is penalized for it. That is wrong. 

Retirement pay reflects years of service and disability benefits reflect injury — they should never cancel each other out. Dr. Turner’s story is why the Major Richard Star Act is so important. 

Thank you for your service!
